idiom_name: empty struct (size 0) + protocol extension default implementations
implementation_notes: Swift value types can be genuinely zero-sized: the layout algorithm starts at size 0 and alignment 1, and zero-sized structs and tuples are allowed and take up no storage in enclosing aggregates, so MemoryLayout<Empty>.size is 0 (its stride is 1 so instances stay addressable). Behaviour belongs to protocols: protocol extensions add default implementations with no stored properties, and conformance adds nothing to the instance layout, which replaces the classic empty-base structure. Structs cannot inherit and a class may have only one base class, so a 'stateless base' is idiomatically an empty struct carrying type-level meaning plus a protocol extension for behaviour; keep classes for identity and state, and protocols for behaviour.
pitfalls: A generic parameter used only as a stateless policy still monomorphises: the compiler may emit a separate specialization per policy type, trading memory for code size.
The stride of an empty type is 1, so arrays and homogeneous tuples of zero-sized values keep distinct addresses and cannot be assumed to be layout-free.
Adding stored properties - in the primary type or via Objective-C associated objects - reintroduces per-instance state, and protocol extensions cannot declare stored properties at all.
